medications.indication: type 2 diabetes mellitus (low dose given CKD stage 2)

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and adult granddaughter
social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 18 years ago

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive walking difficulty, frequent urinary accidents, and worsening memory over 18 months — family concerned
patient.history_present_illness: A 75-year-old retired city bus driver with hypertension, type 2 diabetes on insulin, and CKD stage 2 was admitted for NPH evaluation after progressive functional decline over the past 18 months. He and his wife first noticed his walking became slower and less coordinated about 18 months ago. He describes difficulty 'getting started walking' — once in motion he can walk, but initiating the first steps feels like his feet are 'glued to the floor.' He has had five falls, including one that caused a right wrist sprain. He now uses a four-wheeled rollator walker and requires his wife's assistance for outdoor walks. Urinary urgency and incontinence developed approximately 12 months ago with daily near-accidents and at least four actual incontinence episodes per week. His wife handles his protective underwear. Cognitive changes have been progressive: he forgets grocery lists, cannot recall recent conversations, and has missed insulin doses several times because he forgot whether he had taken it. He has always been a disciplined, schedule-oriented person from his driving career. His granddaughter, who has a nursing background, recognized the classic triad from her training and pushed for neurological evaluation. A head CT three months ago was notable for marked ventriculomegaly (Evans index approximately 0.39 on visual inspection). Renal function is mildly impaired (CKD stage 2 with eGFR 68) which is relevant for contrast administration planning.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place; uncertain of date. MoCA 20/30. Impaired delayed recall (1/5), executive dysfunction (clock drawing — hands placed incorrectly), visuospatial impairment. No aphasia.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone. Full strength in upper extremities. Mild hip flexor weakness bilaterally (4+/5). No resting tremor. No rigidity.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced vibration at bilateral ankles and distal feet — mild. Light touch intact.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact. Heel-shin mildly clumsy bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, severely apraxic shuffling gait. Prominent freezing on initiation. Very short steps. TUG 34 seconds. 10-meter walk 28 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — 3 steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: Bilateral grasp reflexes present. Snout reflex. No nuchal rigidity.

mri.impression: Florid iNPH: Evans index 0.41, callosal angle 68°, prominent DESH, transependymal signal, hyperdynamic aqueductal flow void. Background moderate white matter disease from hypertension and diabetes. Contrast not administered given CKD stage. Clinical correlation recommended.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (H), BUN 24 mg/dL (H), Glucose 138 mg/dL (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 46 mg/dL. Glucose: 70 mg/dL (ratio 0.51). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 724 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 218 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (42 mL) with quantitative gait assessment

findings.urinary: Decreased urgency; no incontinence in 24 hours post-tap

specialized_test.impression: Positive tap trial. TUG improved 35% at 24 hours (34 sec to 22 sec); 10-meter walk improved 36% (28 sec to 18 sec); MoCA improved 3 points (20 to 23). Decreased urgency; no incontinence episode in 24 hours post-tap. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 13, below the threshold of 24. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Reduced amplitude 3.2 mcV (normal >4.5), mildly slow velocity — mild distal axonal sensory neuropathy

output.impression: Mild distal axonal sensory neuropathy. Sural nerve sensory amplitude reduced at 3.2 mcV (reference >4.5 mcV) with mildly slowed velocity. Peroneal and tibial motor responses normal. Pattern is consistent with a length-dependent axonal sensory neuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

Markedly hyperdynamic aqueductal flow. Peak velocity 25 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); stroke volume 90 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Both values substantially exceed published normative ranges. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 118 mL. No outlet obstruction.

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity. Involuntary contractions at 118 mL. No outlet obstruction. Pattern is consistent with detrusor overactivity of neurogenic origin. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: VP shunt surgery in patient with CKD stage 2 on insulin glargine and metformin
interactions: Metformin — hold 48h before elective surgery (risk of lactic acidosis if acute kidney injury perioperatively); resume when oral intake resumed and renal function stable
warnings: Insulin glargine — continue at reduced dose (50% of usual basal) on morning of surgery; hold mealtime boluses until eating
CKD stage 2 — adequate renal function for gadolinium-contrast MRI if needed (eGFR 68 > threshold of 30)
Monitor blood glucose closely perioperatively — target 140-180 mg/dL intraoperatively

output.query: iNPH vs vascular dementia white matter hyperintensities differentiation tap trial

results.title: Distinguishing iNPH from vascular dementia using tap trial
results.key_finding: Positive tap trial (TUG >20%) favors iNPH even in presence of white matter disease; Fazekas 2 WMH does not exclude iNPH or predict poor shunt response

output.summary: In iNPH patients with concurrent white matter hyperintensities, a positive tap trial (TUG >20%) remains predictive of VP shunt response regardless of Fazekas grade. Fazekas 2 WMH does not preclude shunt benefit based on available registry data. Clinical correlation is required.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

cardiac_monitoring.rhythm_summary: Predominant sinus rhythm throughout the recording
findings: Occasional premature atrial complexes, benign. No sustained arrhythmia, no pauses greater than 2 seconds, no AV block.
cardiac_monitoring.impression: 24-hour Holter monitor with only benign findings.

differential.key_features: Moderate WMH (Fazekas 2) from hypertension/diabetes; however Evans 0.41 and strongly positive tap trial confirm NPH dominance

differential.diagnosis: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy causing gait ataxia
differential.key_features: Mild distal axonal neuropathy — insufficient to explain apraxic magnetic gait. NPH is primary.
Normal CSF biomarkers, negative amyloid PET. Frontal-subcortical cognitive pattern.
CKD stage 2, eGFR 68 — far above uremic threshold. Creatinine 1.4 (stable). NPH explains entire syndrome.

optimal_actions.action: Labs (CBC, BMP including creatinine/eGFR, HbA1c, TSH, B12, RPR)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: CKD stage 2 (creatinine 1.4); well-controlled DM (HbA1c 7.6%); normal TSH/B12/RPR

optimal_actions.action: High-volume tap trial (42 mL) with pre/post gait analysis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal OP 15 cmH2O; strongly positive (35% TUG)

optimal_actions.action: NCS/EMG to quantify diabetic neuropathy contribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild axonal sensory neuropathy — not sufficient to explain gait

optimal_actions.action: VP shunt with perioperative metformin hold and insulin adjustment

critical_actions: Hold metformin 48h before VP shunt surgery (CKD + surgical risk)
Reduce insulin glargine dose on day of surgery (50% basal, hold mealtime)
No gadolinium contrast without considering eGFR — eGFR 68 is acceptable for standard protocol
contraindicated_actions: Attributing gait and cognitive decline to CKD — eGFR 68 does not cause encephalopathy
Using gadolinium contrast without confirming eGFR (eGFR 68 — acceptable)
Continuing metformin perioperatively with CKD patient undergoing surgery
key_reasoning_points: Florid iNPH — Evans 0.41, callosal angle 68°, strongly positive tap trial (35%)
CKD stage 2 is a comorbidity requiring medication management but does NOT cause the NPH syndrome
Mild diabetic neuropathy (HbA1c 7.6%) is coincidental — does not explain magnetic apraxic gait
Negative amyloid PET confirms pure iNPH without Alzheimer's copathology

red_herrings.data_point: CKD stage 2 (creatinine 1.4, BUN 24) with cognitive decline
red_herrings.intended_effect: Uremic encephalopathy considered as etiology for cognitive impairment
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: eGFR 68 is far above the threshold for uremic encephalopathy. CKD stage 2 does not cause cognitive impairment. NPH is the primary diagnosis.

red_herrings.data_point: Type 2 DM on insulin with mild distal vibration loss
red_herrings.intended_effect: Gait instability and vibration loss attributed to diabetic peripheral neuropathy
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: NCS shows only mild axonal sensory neuropathy — insufficient to explain wide-based magnetic apraxic gait. NPH is the dominant etiology.

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Straightforward iNPH in a 75-year-old retired bus driver — florid MRI, strongly positive tap trial. CKD stage 2 and diabetic neuropathy as metabolic red herrings requiring perioperative management.
